args.passage_a: Simply dropping the swap would also work, at a median of 86% agreement. Per-triangle orientation also covers the faces whose native winding is locally inconsistent.
args.passage_b: Measured over all 728 GT cars, dropping the swap gives median agreement 0.842 (0.843 for day cars), with one car below one half and 16 at or above 0.99. Per-triangle orientation from stored normals gives median 1.0. About 16.8% of a typical day car's body area has stored normals nearly perpendicular to the face, so neither winding policy orients those faces reliably; on LD7VR a door panel stays dark after either policy until those normals are replaced by geometric face normals.
